body:
Chief: M1'S REDEFINITIONS ARE COMPLETE, landed at merge 7cf9d58, pushed. Gate on the merged tree, unpiped, SBT_EXIT=0, zero errors: align 172/172 on all three platforms, embedBench 52/52, lawsJVM 81/81, interviewJVM 76/76. Bead closed.

WHAT FIDELITY USED TO BE, and it is worth stating because it is two defects that turn out to be one. A unit entered the fidelity calculation only if its source mass exceeded its external mass - a CLIFF AT 0.5, so a unit at 0.51 contributed its verdict at FULL WEIGHT and a unit at 0.49 contributed NOTHING. Then, having admitted it, we scored only its MAP anchor - so a unit split 0.51/0.49 across two anchors was recorded as though the first anchor were certain. Both moves are the same move: collapse a distribution to a point, then treat the point as certain. The mutation number makes it concrete - only TWO of four units cleared the old cliff, so the published fidelity was a mean over two units standing in for a recall of four.

I NEARLY BLOCKED THIS FOR THE WRONG REASON and want that on the record. RecallSignature still has fidelity: Option[Double] sitting next to the new fidelityMass: MassRatio, which looks exactly like the deprecated-twin pattern I forbade when we retired route:transition-direction - a wrong number kept alongside its replacement where someone can still cite it. I checked rather than blocked: line 316 is 'val fidelity = fidelityRatio.value', so the old field is a PROJECTION of the new ratio, not a survival of the old cliff. The cliff that remains at line 272 governs which units get a per-unit FidelityReport, which is a different question from the aggregate.

THERE IS A RESIDUAL AND I AM NOT BLOCKING ON IT. A bare Option[Double] beside a supported MassRatio is an ADR 0003 clause-2 convenience leak: the library offers a way to quote the number without its support, which is precisely what externalMass prevents by refusing to have a sum accessor. It goes when the remaining Option[Double] fields migrate, and it is in the migration backlog rather than a new bead. I blocked a strict improvement for incompleteness once tonight, on this same author's projection fix, and left a worse thing on main for an hour. Not twice.

AND THE TEST LESSON IS NOW A RULE. m1 reported that its FIRST version of the fidelity test did not catch the mutation: conditioningMass != unitCount and conditioningMass <= sourceMass BOTH PASS under the mutant, because the surviving-unit count was 2.0 and the source mass 2.63 - an inequality that happens to hold. The assertion that works recomputes the denominator independently, from a different expression over the same inputs. That is AGENTS.md rule 4 now: AN INEQUALITY IS NOT A DISCRIMINATING ASSERTION. m1 calls it the sixth such survival in one session; six caught by the author, none by me, and all six reported before anyone asked.

m1 has moved to the interview internalRatio bias. Engineer is on embed-core. Scout is on the interview specificity split.
